raw_response:
I've been farming this little plot of 2 mu for forty years now. My father farmed it before me, and I've seen good years and bad years. I'm sixty years old with only primary school education, so I don't know all those technical words the extension people use. I know what I know from doing it myself and from watching Old Wang and Old Li next door.

My son and daughter-in-law both work in the factory in Handan, and they send some money home for the grandchildren. But I don't ask them for money for the farm — this is my responsibility, and 2 mu isn't much but it's what I have. My wife helps me, and sometimes my grandson comes out to help on weekends. We do everything ourselves. Hiring labor costs at least 150 yuan a day now, and on 2 mu there's no margin for that.

This year, same as always, I'll plant wheat on the whole 2 mu in early October, right after I get the maize off. For wheat seed, I saved most of it from last year, but I bought a small bag of new seed from the county store to mix in — old seed gets weak after a while. That cost me about 20 yuan total for the new seed.

For fertilizer, I put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's about one big bag for the whole plot. I work it into the soil when I till. Then in March, at jointing, I watch the color. If it looks a bit yellow, I topdress with urea, maybe 10 kg per mu. I can't afford to put down as much as Old Wang next door — he has 5 mu and his son has a good job in Beijing. But I learned my lesson years ago: if you skimp too much on fertilizer and then the spring is dry, you lose everything. So I put down enough to be safe. I figure about 12–14 kg of nitrogen per mu total for the wheat.

I irrigate twice for wheat — once in late November before winter if it's dry, and once in April at jointing. The well water costs electricity money, and with only 2 mu I have to be careful. But wheat is our main food, so I make sure it doesn't suffer. I spray herbicide once in spring to keep the weeds down — that's about 25 yuan for a bottle that covers my whole plot.

For the maize, the window is tight — sometimes I plant the very next day after wheat harvest in early June. I buy hybrid seed from the county store, 45 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — about 20 kg of compound per mu in the furrow. No time for split application, and anyway the maize season is short. I irrigate once in July if it doesn't rain. Summer rains usually help, and I save on the electricity.

My wife and I can handle all the labor. Planting takes a day, harvesting takes a day for each crop, and in between it's just weeding, watching, and irrigating. Total maybe eleven days of family labor across the whole year for the 2 mu.

I expect about 380 kg per mu for wheat and 420 kg per mu for maize if the weather is normal. Last year was okay, not great. I don't expect miracles — I just need enough grain for the family and a little to sell. My total costs this year are about 420 yuan. That's a lot for me, but if I don't spend it, I won't get anything back.
